text:
NJD arrive on a five-game winning streak, the latest a 4-0 win at TOR on Nov. 8 in which Nico Hischier reached 500 career points. They're without Anthony Mantha (neck), with Connor Brown moving in beside Rodrigues and Boqvist. WPG have won three straight, most recently 4-3 over TBL, where Brayden Yager scored his first NHL goal. They're missing Josh Morrissey, whose minutes are going to Mario Ferraro and Neal Pionk. It's also Dawson Mercer's first game against the Devils since leaving them.

Our numbers favor New Jersey. At five on five, NJD have taken 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in their games, against 47% for WPG, and our model projects 3.51 goals for the Devils to 2.80 for the Jets. The power play is the one even spot: both create 0.82 expected goals a game, though WPG's penalty kill allows 0.86 to NJD's 0.44.

Neither projected goalie has been sharp. Jake Allen (NJD) is at -4.74 goals saved above expected, which measures saves against the quality of shots faced, and Nico Daws (WPG) is at -1.28. Allen was at +5.39 last season over 37 games.

For NJD, Jack Hughes has a 42% chance to score and 80% to record a point, on a five-game point streak. Jesper Bratt, who won it in overtime against STL, is at 25% to score. For WPG, Kyle Connor is at 44% to score, with seven points in his last five games per RotoWire.
